name: Light Aquamarine
lede: Light Aquamarine is a near-neon, pale green-blue built from the word "light" plus [[aquamarine|Aquamarine]], the sea-and-gemstone color, and a 2010 crowd survey put this exact swatch on record.

sections.title: A modifier on a gemstone word
sections.body:
The name follows the usual grammar: "light" plus the parent color [[aquamarine|Aquamarine]], itself named for the pale blue-green of seawater and the gem beryl colored by traces of iron [1]. Our graph credits the 2010 xkcd color survey for this exact, brighter and paler swatch, distinct from the gem's own calmer, more muted range [1]. By computed ISCC-NBS block it lands as a very light green [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is the parent itself, [[aquamarine|Aquamarine]], only 2.7 units away, with [[light-greenish-blue|Light Greenish Blue]] close behind at 3.3, and [[greenish-cyan|Greenish Cyan]] and [[light-seafoam|Light Seafoam]] further out at 4.8 and 4.9 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, within a color distance of 4, as photographed [2]. The real gem and real seawater never reach a green this bright and saturated, so the gap in the archive reflects a modern, screen-only brightness rather than any gap in our data [2].

notes.cite: ColorHub color graph: xkcd 2010 crowd color survey and look-alike edges
ColorHub archive (23,781 paintings), computed match, as photographed

questions.q: Light Aquamarine is a brighter, paler version of which parent color?
True or false: real aquamarine gemstones reach a green as bright and saturated as this swatch.

openers: Light Aquamarine is brighter than any real gemstone or seawater actually gets.
